title: Extracting Nucleic Acids from Viruses on a Filter
author: Grieg F. Steward and Alexander I. Culley
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.dsm6c5
materials: Allow the syringe-filter assembly to cool briefly.

steps.title: Prepare injection syringe with lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL T + C lysis buffer containing 100 µg/mL proteinase K to a low‑volume (1–3 cc) syringe fitted with a female‑female Luer‑Lok adapter (the injection syringe). If desired, use a larger (10–20 cc) syringe as a buffer reservoir; fill the injection syringe by tip‑to‑tip connection via the adapter. The reservoir can fill multiple injection syringes for multiple samples.

steps.title: Assemble syringe‑filter extraction system
steps.instruction: Ensure minimal air in the injection syringe‑adapter assembly, then connect it to the filter outlet. Connect a second low‑volume syringe to the filter inlet (aspiration syringe). Hold the filter‑syringe assembly vertically with the injector syringe pushing upward from below, and gently push extraction buffer into the filter housing until liquid just begins to appear in the aspiration syringe.

steps.title: Incubate filter assembly at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Place the assembled filter with both syringes in a hybridization oven (or on a rotisserie) and incubate for 15 min at 65 °C. If using a rotisserie, secure the syringes to the clips with elastic bands to keep the filter surface wetted and to eliminate bubbles.

steps.title: Collect extract into aspiration syringe
steps.instruction: Hold the assembly vertically with the aspiration syringe underneath (filter upside down) and gently pull the plunger to draw the extract into the aspiration syringe.

steps.title: Transfer extract to microcentrifuge tube
steps.instruction: Dispense the collected extract into a microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with MPC reagent
steps.instruction: Add one‑half volume of MPC protein precipitation reagent (supplied in the kit) to the extract and vortex for 10 s.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 10,000 g for 10 min to pellet debris.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and optional freeze
steps.instruction: Transfer the clear supernatant to a sterile microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the pellet. Optionally archive the sample by freezing at –80 °C.

steps.title: Add carrier and isopropanol for precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 800 µL of the supernatant to a fresh tube, add 1 µL polyacryl carrier (optional, improves yields for nanogram‑to‑subnanogram nucleic‑acid amounts), and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Mix with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 100 % isopropanol and invert the tube several times to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at ≥10,000 g for 15–45 min (longer times improve yield for low‑quantity samples, especially without carrier).

steps.title: Remove supernatant carefully
steps.instruction: Decant or aspirate the supernatant carefully, avoiding loss of the easily dislodged pellet.

steps.title: Air‑dry and resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet, then dissolve it in 10 µL of 0.5× TE buffer (0.02‑ filtered, sterile) pre‑heated to 50 °C.

steps.title: Optional enzymatic removal of DNA or RNA
steps.instruction: If required, selectively digest DNA or RNA from the total nucleic‑acid precipitate using DNase or RNase, respectively.
